exposure: Mode of birth (elective/planned Cesarean section, normal vaginal delivery)
outcome: Neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) stay duration
cohort: The cohort consisted of 205 term newborns (gestational age > 37 weeks) born by either elective/planned Cesarean section or normal vaginal delivery at maternity teaching hospitals in Mosul City, excluding premature births or those whose mothers had health problems during pregnancy.
finding: Neonates born via Cesarean section had a significantly higher incidence of respiratory distress (44.2%) compared to those born via normal vaginal delivery (11.8%).
mod_finding: Babies born via elective or planned Cesarean section had a higher risk of respiratory distress and longer stays in the neonatal intensive care unit compared to babies born via normal vaginal delivery.
